sentences.text: The genus name Muiscasaurus honors the Muisca people of central Colombia and the Greek word for reptile. This animal possessed a compact, streamlined body with a half-moon shaped tail and flipper-like limbs.

The known fossils represent a juvenile individual based on incomplete bone formation and skull proportions. The preserved skull is 45 cm long, with total cranial length estimated between 48 and 65 cm. Muiscasaurus is distinguished by a very thin premaxilla and a nasal aperture partially divided into two ovals by a spur-shaped process.
Its teeth were very thin and lacked the thick enamel and coarse striations found in similar ichthyosaurs like Pervushovisaurus and Platypterygius.
While the juvenile was about 3 meters long, adults could have reached up to 5 meters in length.

Fossils of Muiscasaurus were discovered in the Paja Formation near Villa de Leyva in the Boyacá Department of Colombia. The remains were found in 2010 inside a limestone concretion within the Arcillolitas abigarradas Member.
The genus and species Muiscasaurus catheti were formally described in 2015.
Analysis suggests Muiscasaurus was a specialized predator feeding on smaller, softer prey, unlike the generalist diet of its relative Kyhytysuka.
Muiscasaurus is classified within the family Ophthalmosauridae. Phylogenetic analysis suggests Muiscasaurus occupies a very basal position within the Ophthalmosauridae family.
Muiscasaurus lived in modern Colombia during the Early Cretaceous period. Muiscasaurus lived between 125.77 and 113.2 million years ago during the Barremian to Aptian stages.
The precise age of the specimen was difficult to establish because attached ammonites were too poorly preserved to identify.
